answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by counting endorsement diversity, not endorsement volume. A new identity starts at the nadir of trust and gains influence only when vouched for by peers with no shared history, no common sponsors, and no overlapping work trails, like separate embers rather than one fire split into sparks. A Sybil farm can mint thousands of identities, but if they all endorse each other, the graph collapses them into a single summit of influence, so the attacker pays full fabrication cost for one vote. Honest newcomers climb slowly through genuinely independent sponsors.
